title: Kimbap: A Node-Property Map System for Distributed Graph Analytics
problem: Existing distributed graph analytics systems only support computational models where node properties are updated using adjacent neighbor properties, preventing expression of algorithms like Louvain for community detection and Shiloach-Vishkin for connected components.
motivation: These restricted algorithms may be less efficient or produce lower quality results than algorithms with more flexible property access patterns.
method: Kimbap introduces a Node-Property Map computational abstraction that generalizes beyond neighbor-only updates to support more flexible property access patterns during iterative graph computation while maintaining distributed parallel execution.
key_novelty: Generalized computational model that expands expressible algorithms in distributed graph systems beyond neighbor-based updates.
contributions: Node-Property Map abstraction for distributed graph analytics
System enabling previously inexpressible algorithms like Louvain and Shiloach-Vishkin
Framework supporting both efficiency and output quality improvements

metrics.other: Algorithm efficiency and output quality improvements

limitations: Specific performance metrics and implementation details not discussed in abstract
primary_theme: Generalized computation model for graph analytics
